t: Batting for the Milwaukee Braves against Vic Raschi of the St. Louis Cardinals, Hank Aaron hit the first of his 755 home runs in Major League Baseball.
At Oxford's Iffley Road Track, English runner Roger Bannister became the first person to run the mile in under four minutes.
A convoy of circus wagons carrying lions, horses, ponies and an ass lost control and overturned into some shop fronts in Dungannon, Northern Ireland.

The U.S. Supreme Court ruled in the landmark case Brown v. Board of Education, outlawing racial segregation in public schools because "separate educational facilities are inherently unequal" and therefore unconstitutional.
The security clearance of American nuclear physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer, head of Project Y, was revoked.
Diane Leather became the first woman to run a mile in less than five minutes.

During hearings investigating conflicting accusations between the United States Army and Senator Joseph McCarthy, Army lawyer Joseph N. Welch asked McCarthy: "At long last, have you left no sense of decency?"
Dominic Savio, who was 14 years old at his death in 1857, was canonized by Pope Pius XII, making him one of the youngest non-martyred saints in the Catholic Church.
Carlos Castillo Armas led a CIA-sponsored invasion force across the Guatemalan border, beginning the 1954 Guatemalan coup d'état.
Jacobo Árbenz resigned as President of Guatemala following a CIA-led coup against his administration.
In what is known as "The Miracle of Bern", West Germany defeated Hungary 3–2 to win the FIFA World Cup.
Elvis Presley recorded his first single, "That's All Right", at Sun Records in Memphis, Tennessee.
A limited state of martial law was declared in Russell County, Alabama, due to organized crime.
The Fellowship of the Ring, the first part of J. R. R. Tolkien's novel The Lord of the Rings, was published by Allen & Unwin.
A team of Italian climbers became the first to reach the summit of K2, the world's second-highest mountain.
The Cruise of the Kings, a royal cruise organised by the Queen Consort of Greece, Frederica of Hanover, departed from Marseille, France.
In the midst of a political crisis, Brazilian president Getúlio Vargas fatally shot himself in the Catete Palace in Rio de Janeiro.
Eight nations signed a collective-defense treaty in Manila to create the Southeast Asia Treaty Organization, modelled on NATO.
A magnitude-6.7 earthquake struck near Chlef, killing over 1,200 people and forcing the Algerian government to implement comprehensive reforms in building codes.
The scene in The Seven Year Itch of Marilyn Monroe standing in a white dress over a subway grate was filmed by Billy Wilder.
Willie Mays of the New York Giants made The Catch, one of the most famous defensive plays in the history of Major League Baseball.
Hurricane Hazel made landfall in the Carolinas in the United States before moving north to Toronto in Canada later the same day, killing 176 people in the two countries.
The first film featuring the giant monster Godzilla was released nationwide in Japan.
A meteorite crashed through a roof in Sylacauga, Alabama, and hit a sleeping woman in the first verified case of a human being injured by an extraterrestrial object.
The United States Senate voted of 67 to 22 to approve a resolution condemning Senator Joseph McCarthy who continued to serve in the Senate until his death two and a half years later.
The Finnish National Bureau of Investigation was established to consolidate criminal investigation and intelligence into a single agency.
